questions.question: Some underwriters are credited differently in DSR and RBS - which is right?
questions.today: Each report's own underwriter columns are used. On the real data one underwriter has 3 DSR submissions but 22 RBS binds (a 733% win rate, shown greyed as "few quotes"): their bound business is credited to them in RBS but mostly to someone else in DSR.
questions.options: Credit binds by DSR's underwriter where the policy is in both, as New/Renewal already follows one report.

questions.question: Headline premium: RBS (ours) or DSR (Matt's)?
questions.today: RBS, with DSR as a cross-check (9.1% apart on Jan–Aug 2026 - flagged). Matt's headline premium is the DSR one, and his per-head and deal-size figures sit on that base, so his headline figure is our cross-check figure.
questions.options: Match Matt and lead with DSR premium; or keep RBS and expect a gap when comparing with his deck.

questions.question: GELR: should 2021 inceptions be left out, as Matt's does?
questions.today: Every year in the filters is included.
questions.options: Drop 2021 inceptions from GELR (and say why), as his tooltip says his does.

questions.question: Blank or zero commission counts as "none charged" - should it?
questions.today: Counted as 0% in both the book and the margin version, while a blank or zero GELR is treated as unusable and left out. So the two halves of 100 - GELR - Commission handle a missing value in opposite ways, and UW Margin % reads high: 11.5% of the margin premium records no commission; margin reads 44.4% and 43.0% over the rows that do record one. The page now says this under the figure.
questions.options: Leave rows with no recorded commission out of the margin version too (as GELR does); or keep the current rule and rely on the note.

questions.question: Should B/Q and B/S only count binds that DSR knows about?
questions.today: They divide RBS binds by DSR quotes / submissions, as tab 4 defines. But the funnel isn't nested: 169 of 5,034 bound policies (9.0% of premium) have no DSR row at all; B/Q reads 43.8% and would read 42.3% without them. On a narrow slice or one underwriter the rate can pass 100% (the page flags that). Matt's build doesn't have this problem because his binds come from DSR too.
questions.options: Restrict the numerator to binds present in DSR (a true funnel, slightly lower); or keep RBS binds and rely on the note.

questions.question: Entity is recorded per line in RBS but per policy in DSR
questions.today: The entity filter keeps matching LINES, so a policy whose lines sit under two entities is counted as a bind under each while only its own lines' premium is summed: 99 policies in scope have lines under more than one entity, so binds summed over the 12 entities come to 5,183 against 5,034 actual (+3.0%). Average Deal Size for a small entity can therefore read far below the book figure.
questions.options: Assign each policy to one entity (e.g. the one with most premium) before counting binds; or leave it and note that entity slices don't add up to the total.

questions.question: A few extreme rate changes set RARC
questions.today: RARC is a premium-weighted average with no cap: 48 rows book-wide are beyond ±300% (largest 2,965%); dropping the in-scope ones moves RARC by about 1.7 points. The refresh now logs a warning naming how many rows are beyond the limit.
questions.options: Leave them out, or cap them, once someone confirms whether they are real.

questions.question: Should rates built on very few deals be hidden or flagged?
questions.today: Shown, but greyed out with a "few binds / few quotes / few submissions" tag when they rest on fewer than 20 policies - and per-person figures with a "few underwriters" tag below 5 underwriters. Nothing is hidden (tab 4: blank only when there's nothing to divide by).
questions.options: Hide below a minimum instead; or change the minimums.

questions.options: Matt's build mixes submission-month DSR with inception-month RBS.

questions.options: Only themselves (always reads 1.0x).

questions.options: Per line counts long multi-line policies several times.

questions.question: Renewal Premium Growth with the Business filter on New?

questions.today: Excess: blank left out. Primary: blank deductible counts as 0, per the tab 4 note - which is worth revisiting, because it halves the figure: 29,274 ours (blank = 0) vs 58,547 if blanks were left out (Jan–Aug 2026).

versus.matt: Adds up the premium on the DSR policy rows, and applies RBS's margin % to that DSR premium, so his headline stays consistent with the funnel it came from.
versus.ours: Adds up the premium on the RBS rows. DSR's bound-row total is worked out too, but only as a cross-check with a red badge.
versus.worth: 9.1% apart on Jan–Aug 2026 - flagged
versus.which: RBS. It is the company's source of truth for bound business (tab 3, Rule 7), and the gap is measured and shown rather than hidden. Matt's is internally consistent with his funnel, so his headline figure is our cross-check figure - open question 23.

versus.matt: Counts distinct DSR policies whose status marks them bound.
versus.ours: Counts distinct policies in RBS. DSR's own count is the cross-check.
versus.worth: 3.4% apart on Jan–Aug 2026 - flagged
versus.which: RBS, same reason as premium. Both treat a mid-term cancellation as bound.

versus.matt: Average monthly employed headcount from the HR file, filtered by entity, line, ROLE and TENURE. For one underwriter: the share of the window HR has them employed. Falls back to a producing roster where a slice has no HR figure.
versus.ours: No HR file: Active underwriters (won at least one deal, from RBS) and Roster underwriters (at least one submission, from DSR). Both are producer counts.
versus.worth: Not measurable here - we have no HR file to compare against.
versus.which: Ours is the only honest option without HR, and every figure built on it is labelled a stand-in (tab 1, point 5). Matt's is true employed headcount and is better wherever HR exists. His own note warns his default New + Open Market slice divides 56% of the premium by 100% of the heads ($2.09M per head, against $3.72M on all business).

versus.section: SAME DEFINITION - FIGURES SHOULD LINE UP (once the premium base above is allowed for)

versus.matt: Margin premium ÷ premium carrying a GELR; equals 1 − margin GELR − margin commission exactly.
versus.ours: 100% − margin GELR − margin commission, over rows with a usable GELR.
versus.worth: Same arithmetic.
versus.which: Both; neither subtracts Mosaic's internal commission (open question 2).

versus.matt: His single "GELR" figure: premium-weighted over GELR-bearing rows.
versus.ours: Our margin version - same population.
versus.worth: Same, except he also drops 2021 inceptions and we don't (open question 24).
versus.which: Both. Ours is named "margin version" so it can't be confused with the book version.

versus.matt: His single "Commission" figure: premium-weighted over ALL premium, blank counting as no commission.
versus.ours: Our book version - same population and same blank rule.
versus.worth: 16.55% ours vs 18.69% over only the rows that carry a commission
versus.which: Both.

versus.matt: Margin premium ÷ all premium; and the share of margin premium carrying a commission above zero (his note: 12.2% carries exactly zero).
versus.ours: The same two figures, same populations.
versus.worth: Same arithmetic.
versus.which: Both.

versus.matt: 1 − Mosaic 1609's premium ÷ all agency premium - a ratio of sums, not an average of percentages.
versus.ours: The same.
versus.worth: Same arithmetic.
versus.which: Both.

versus.matt: Share of ROWS (a small deal counts the same as a large one).
versus.ours: Share of rows too.
versus.worth: Row count vs premium-weighted: 52.0% ours (rows) vs 54.1% weighted by premium for primary share.
versus.which: Both, with the row-count caveat written next to the figure. Which Slip Lead values count as "Mosaic" is still open (question 19).

versus.matt: Renewals only whatever the business-type filter says, weighted by expiring premium; every other filter still applies.
versus.ours: The same.
versus.worth: Same arithmetic.
versus.which: Both.

versus.matt: Distinct policies for submissions, quotes and binds; a rate is blank, never zero, when there is nothing to divide by.
versus.ours: The same rule.
versus.worth: Structure agrees; the levels differ because his binds come from DSR (see above).
versus.which: Both.

versus.matt: Distinct producing underwriters across the filtered policy rows, any status - his fallback denominator.
versus.ours: Our Roster underwriters - the same definition.
versus.worth: Same arithmetic.
versus.which: Both.

versus.figure: Last 12 months, and the month still in progress
versus.matt: Re-indexes every row onto a window ending at the last complete month; the month bar is fixed under that window and the part month is marked.
versus.ours: A window of twelve months ending at the last complete month; months with no complete data are shown dashed and a notice warns when a period includes them.
versus.worth: Same rule, different mechanics.
versus.which: Both.

versus.matt: All the premium in scope ÷ a benchmark built only from rows that have one: `adequacy: bn? agwp/bn`.
versus.ours: Premium and benchmark restricted to the same rows (usable GELR and a plan loss ratio above 0).
versus.worth: 139.7% ours vs 140.4% Matt-style (all premium over the same benchmark)
versus.which: Ours. His numerator includes premium that contributed nothing to the denominator, which overstates it - the workbook flagged this from the start (tab 4). We also show RBS's own benchmark premium as a second opinion.

versus.matt: Doesn't exist - he shows one GELR only.
versus.ours: An extra version: premium-weighted across all rows, a blank GELR counting as 0.
versus.worth: 38.80% ours vs 39.01% if blanks were left out
versus.which: Both of ours are shown, each clearly named, because tab 4 asks for the "across all rows" reading. Whether a blank should count as 0 is open question 1.

versus.matt: Weights by premium but divides by ALL premium in scope, so a premium-bearing row with no line share recorded drags it down.
versus.ours: Uses only the rows that have a line share, on both sides of the division.
versus.worth: Not directly measurable (we don't hold his figure), but it is the same class of error he fixed elsewhere in his own code for fees and margin.
versus.which: Ours. A share can only be averaged over risks that have one.

versus.matt: One column, Excess + Deductible added together, then split by layer and medianed.
versus.ours: Excess only on Excess layers (blanks left out); Deductible only on Primary layers (blank = 0).
versus.worth: 29,274 ours (blank = 0) vs 58,547 if blanks were left out
versus.which: Ours keeps the two ideas apart, which is easier to explain. The blank-as-zero rule is the workbook's (tab 4) and halves the Primary figure - worth revisiting.

versus.matt: A median of Agency Exposure - but his label says "Avg limit" and his own tooltip says "mean".
versus.ours: The same median, named "Median limit" on screen.
versus.worth: median 5,854,701 ours vs mean 17,832,668 (what "Average Limit" would suggest)
versus.which: Ours. Same arithmetic, honest name - a mean would read three times higher.

versus.matt: Annualised UW margin per underwriter, against the median of their PRODUCT or line, leaving the person out of their own median, annualised by months employed from HR, with a membership rule that drops thin or out-of-entity names and seeds rows for leavers.
versus.ours: Premium against the median premium of everyone in the current filters (the person included), leaving out anyone with no premium. No annualisation.
versus.worth: Peer median $3.24M ours (zero-premium underwriters left out).
versus.which: His is better on every axis he gives a reason for, but most of it needs HR months and a product mapping we don't have. Ours is a stand-in, and the table says so. Open question 10.

versus.matt: The waterfall his page draws allocates each driver's share by Shapley value over every ordering, and carries a fifth margin term. (His code also holds a simpler log-share bridge, which is what ours matches.)
versus.ours: Four drivers, each share = its log change ÷ the total log change, so the shares add to the total exactly.
versus.worth: Same four drivers and the same total; the split between them will differ from his screen.
versus.which: Ours, for now: it is exact, order-independent and easy to explain. A Shapley split and a margin term are a fair next step.

versus.matt: Greys out table ratios below his minimums (e.g. 5 deals).
versus.ours: Greys out any figure resting on fewer than 20 policies, or per-person figures below 5 underwriters, and tags it. Nothing is ever hidden.
versus.worth: Same intent, wider coverage.
versus.which: Ours - tab 9, question 4.

versus.matt: New business, Open Market - the slice his LOB workbook reconciles to.
versus.ours: The whole book.
versus.worth: His default divides 56% of premium by 100% of heads (his own note).
versus.which: Ours, because our denominator follows the filters. One line in config/settings.py to match his - open question 5.

versus.matt: No: his binds come from DSR too, so every bind is also a submission and the funnel is nested by construction.
versus.ours: It can, on a narrow slice: our binds come from RBS and some bound policies have no DSR row at all. The page flags it and says what the rate would be without them.
versus.worth: 169 of 5,034 bound policies (9.0% of premium) have no DSR row at all; B/Q reads 43.8% and would read 42.3% without them
versus.which: Ours keeps RBS as the source of truth for wins, which matters more than a tidy funnel - but this is the strongest argument for his choice. Open question 26.

versus.figure: Agency Revenue, fee yields, fee streams
versus.matt: Total Fees, Syndicate and SCM fees, yields on the fee-bearing premium, and a per-head revenue figure.
versus.ours: Not built - the columns don't exist in the standard RBS export (tab 6).
versus.which: Nothing to follow until the columns exist. His two design points are worth copying then: divide a yield by the premium of the fee-bearing rows only, and split each stream by its own premium.

versus.matt: A product roster and Lloyd's risk-code mapping; HR role and tenure applied to BOTH the premium and the headcount.
versus.ours: Not available (tab 7).
versus.which: Needs his mapping and the HR file - open questions 6 and 7.

versus.matt: UW margin in dollars, index against the line average, a 12-month rolling view, written verdicts per underwriter, prize / sensitivity figures, a CEO three-term test, first-year fallback cards, and a count of names HR can't identify.
versus.ours: Not built.
versus.which: Worth revisiting once the HR file exists; the rolling view is the closest to our Trends tab.

versus.ours: Bound premium and bind count worked out from both reports on the same filters, with a 2% tolerance, a warning in the log and a red badge you can click.
versus.worth: 9.1% apart on Jan–Aug 2026 - flagged
versus.which: Tab 3, Rule 6.

versus.ours: Where a policy is in both reports and they disagree, DSR takes RBS's Renewal Status.
versus.worth: 271 DSR policies changed across the whole extract.
versus.which: Tab 3, Rule 2.

versus.figure: Unit and sanity checks on the way in
versus.ours: Percent columns detected as fractions or percent (the run stops if they disagree), a GELR sanity range, warnings when a value can't be read, and a cache keyed on the file itself.
versus.worth: See tab 13.
versus.which: Tab 13.

versus.ours: Capitals, punctuation and spacing tidied for matching, and likely same-person pairs tagged without merging them.
versus.worth: 4 pairs flagged: Deutsch, Ze'ev / Deutsch, Zeev; Hirst, Justin / Hurst, Justin; Macdonald, Noelle / Macdonald, Nolle; Stedman, Rob / Stedman, Robert
versus.which: Tab 3, Rule 5; open question 8.

versus.ours: Every figure traced to its original columns (tabs 10-11), shown on the page behind an (i), and rebuilt from those raw columns by an automatic check.
versus.worth: Pass - exact match, every figure and every underwriter
versus.which: Tabs 10, 11 and 13.

versus.ours: Rate Adequacy double-check (RBS's own benchmark), Broker concentration, Average policy length, Renewal premium growth, New vs. Renewal and Placement mixes, and the Active / Roster underwriter pair.
versus.which: Tab 5 ideas, all built (tab 8).

versus.section: WORTH KNOWING IF YOU RECONCILE FIGURES WITH HIM

versus.figure: Matt's own labels disagree with his code in three places
versus.matt: Rate adequacy is described three different ways (one tooltip states the reciprocal of what the code does); the limit tile says "Avg" and its tooltip says "mean" while the code takes a median; an "active months" tooltip describes a denominator his peer table only falls back to.
versus.ours: Our definitions are generated from one place (metrics/lineage.py) and shown on the page, so the label and the code can't drift apart.
versus.which: If a figure of his doesn't match ours, check his label against his code before assuming the data differs.

filters.choices: Quick picks: This year so far / Last 12 months / Full year. A quarter: Q1-Q4. Or tick any months.
filters.matt: Partly - YTD / TTM and a month bar
filters.note: "This year so far" = January to the last COMPLETE month (data as at 15 Sep 2026 -> Jan-Aug). "Last 12 months" = the twelve months ending with the last complete month (Sep 2025-Aug 2026). Months with no complete data yet are shown dashed. Ticking a month switches to picked months; choosing a quick pick or quarter clears the ticks.
filters.where: PERIODS in server/filters.py; Scope in scope/filter.py

filters.what: Which year to look at. Always compared with the year before, same months.
filters.choices: Every year in the data up to today (2021-2026)
filters.note: In the Period menu. Looking at a past year uses the same months, so 2024 "This year so far" is Jan-Aug 2024 vs Jan-Aug 2023.

filters.filter: Date basis ("Count a policy in the month of its...")
filters.what: Which date decides the month a policy belongs to.
filters.note: In the Period menu. Tab 3, Rule 3: RBS has no submission date. On Submission, only DSR-only figures are shown (Submissions, Quotes, Quote rate, Roster underwriters); everything needing RBS is blank with a note, rather than quietly mixing two different months. Matt's build mixes them.

filters.what: New business, renewals, or both. Each choice is explained in the menu.
filters.note: Follows RBS's Renewal Status where DSR disagrees (tab 3, Rule 2). RARC and Renewal Premium Growth always look at renewals, whatever is picked here. Matt's build opens on New.

filters.what: How the business reached us. Each choice is explained in the menu.
filters.note: Our data also has Agreement business, which Matt's list doesn't show. Matt's build opens on Open Market because that's what his LOB workbook reconciles to - see tab 9.

filters.what: One class of business, e.g. Cyber.
filters.choices: Only what exists with the other filters
filters.note: Same values on DSR and RBS (tab 3, Rule 2).

filters.what: One producing entity, e.g. Mosaic UK.
filters.choices: Only what exists with the other filters
filters.note: DSR's spellings mapped onto RBS's ("Mosaic Syndicate 2610" -> "Mosaic 2610"). Our data has 12 entities, including syndicates (1609, 2610, 5399, 5431); Matt's list has 7 office entities, so he may group them - open question in tab 9.

filters.what: A product within a line, e.g. Cyber Tech, W&I Tax.
filters.note: Not in DSR or RBS. Matt's build takes it from a product roster and Lloyd's Risk Code mapping we don't have. Listed under "Not available yet" with the reason. Needs that mapping - tab 9.

filters.what: One underwriter. Also: click a name in the Underwriters table.
filters.choices: Searchable list - type part of a name
filters.note: Names matched after tidying capitals, punctuation and spaces only (tab 3, Rule 5). Real duplicates seen: "Stedman, Rob" / "Stedman, Robert", "Hirst, Justin" / "Hurst, Justin". Picking a name keeps the peer comparison against everyone else in the other filters.
Only in the HR file. Listed under "Not available yet".
Only in the HR file. Listed under "Not available yet". Bands already in TENURE_BANDS.

filters.what: Choices take effect when you press Apply. Cancel, Esc or clicking away throws away changes you haven't applied.
filters.note: Each new combination takes 1-2 seconds to work out, so setting three filters used to mean three waits. The page fades while it updates.

filters.what: Each list only offers choices that exist with the other filters, and says how many (e.g. "162 available with your other filters").
filters.note: Built from both reports, this period and last year's. If a change makes a picked name impossible, it's cleared and the page says so, instead of showing an empty page.

filters.what: Type to narrow a list (Underwriter, and any list over 12 choices).
filters.note: "All" and the current choice always stay visible while searching.

filters.what: Every filter that's on shows under the toolbar; × removes just that one.
filters.note: Clear all goes back to the defaults in config/settings.py (DEFAULT_...).

filters.what: The filters are in the page address, e.g. /?period=q2&bt=New&lob=Cyber.
filters.note: Bookmark or paste a filtered view. A broken or old link falls back to defaults rather than showing wrong numbers.
